question: What do we know about the generational wealth transfer, and how are these five preparing for it?

cells.label: fact

items.text: Edward Jones offers eligible retiring financial advisors individually tailored retirement transition plans, which compensate a retiring financial advisor for successfully providing client transition services in accordance with a retirement and transition agreement.
items.quote: Eligible retiring financial advisors are offered individually tailored retirement transition plans. Each retirement transition plan compensates a retiring financial advisor for successfully providing client transition services in accordance with a retirement and transition agreement.

items.text: Generally, the retirement and transition agreement is for five years: during the first two years the retiring financial advisor remains an employee and provides client transition services, retires at the end of year two, and is subject to a non-compete agreement for three years.
items.quote: Generally, the retirement and transition agreement is for five years. During the first two years the retiring financial advisor remains an employee and provides client transition services. The financial advisor retires at the end of year two and is subject to a non-compete agreement for three years.

items.text: Most retiring financial advisors participating in a retirement transition plan are paid ratably over four years; compensation expense is generally recognized ratably over the two-year transition period, with some plans recognized over one year depending on the size and complexity of the transition plan.
items.quote: Most retiring financial advisors participating in a retirement transition plan are paid ratably over four years. Compensation expense is generally recognized ratably over the two-year transition period which aligns with the service period of most agreements, with compensation expense related to some plans recognized over one year depending on the size and complexity of the transition plan.

items.text: The Partnership's comprehensive onboarding program for financial advisors is delivered through online self-paced modules, concentrated application at home office training facilities or a virtual classroom, and on-the-job training in a nearby branch office, with in-region mentorship, training and coaching from field-based leaders and other financial advisors.
items.quote: The Partnership maintains a comprehensive onboarding program for financial advisors delivered through online self-paced modules, concentrated application in one of the Partnership's home office training facilities or a virtual classroom with their peers, and on-the-job training in their respective markets in a nearby branch office. ... Multiple field-based leaders and other financial advisors provide in-region mentorship, training and coaching to financial advisor trainees to assist their assimilation into the Firm and the industry.

items.text: The Partnership also focuses on continuous learning, supporting financial advisors and their teams on building their acumen through professional designations and learning opportunities beyond onboarding.
items.quote: The Partnership also focuses on continuous learning, supporting financial advisors and their teams on building their acumen through professional designations and learning opportunities beyond onboarding.

items.text: Edward Jones' financial advisor attrition increased to 6.4% in the second quarter of 2025 primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends.
items.quote: Financial advisor attrition increased to 6.4% primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends.
items.definition: Attrition % represents the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.

items.text: Edward Jones' financial advisor attrition was 6.1% in the third quarter of 2025 as a result of a variety of factors, including a rise in financial advisor departures with tenure of five years or less.
items.quote: Financial advisor attrition was 6.1% as a result of a variety of factors, including a rise in financial advisor departures with tenure of five years or less.
items.definition: Attrition % represents the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.

items.text: Ken Hullings is not an Edward Jones executive; the attribution in this passage is to LPL regarding SteadRock, not Edward Jones.

cells.reason: The passages describe Edward Jones' retirement transition plans for retiring financial advisors, its advisor onboarding/training programs, and its financial advisor attrition metrics related to retirements, which directly address how the firm prepares for advisor succession and retirement given an aging advisor force.
